fundamental.thesis: ICICI Bank is India's second-largest private sector lender by assets (₹23.7L cr standalone; ₹29.1L cr consolidated), with a diversified retail-focused loan book and a management team with a demonstrated track record of disciplined, risk-calibrated growth. Q4FY26 consolidated PAT grew 9.3% YoY; revenue growth has decelerated from +9.2% to +7.6% across recent filing windows, yet asset quality improved materially — GNPA fell to 1.40% (from 1.58% in H1-FY26) and net NPA reached a best-in-class 0.33%, with credit cost benign at just 38 bps and PCR strong at 75.8%. Using P/B + ROE — the correct yardstick for lenders per the sector card — P/B of 2.48× against ROE of 16.4% grades as FAIR: not cheap (peer-relative P/B ranks P93, a 69% premium to the sector median driven by quality justifiably), not expensive (P/B > 3× with ROE < 12% would be the expensive threshold; ICICI clears both tests), and trailing P/E of 16.82× sits at the upper end of the 12–18× sector range while forward P/E of 13.82× signals ~18–20% expected EPS growth ahead. The single biggest structural risk is that deposit growth (11.4% YoY) continues to lag loan growth (15.8% YoY), tightening the funding gap and forcing reliance on costlier wholesale borrowings; management has already guided NIMs 'range-bound' in FY27, capping the benefit from the ongoing RBI easing cycle and constraining NII upside.

fundamental.thesis: TCS is India's largest IT services company and a global Tier-1 player, generating ₹267,021 cr in FY26 revenue (+4.6% YoY in INR) with ₹49,210 cr PAT (+1.4% YoY), operating at a 4-year-high 25% operating margin backed by a record $40.7B full-year TCV and $2.3B in annualized AI revenues. INR revenue growth accelerated from +1.3% (Q1FY26) to +4.6% (FY26), but this masks a critical -2.4% constant-currency decline — CMT contracted -14% YoY, largely offsetting BFSI's healthy +9.1% growth; PAT margin contracted from 20.1% (Q1FY26) to a trend average of 18.4% before recovering to 19.8% in Q4, reflecting wage-increment pressure and restructuring costs (₹1,300 cr one-offs in FY26). At a trailing P/E of 16.3x versus IT sector median 22-30x and EV/EBITDA of 11.1x versus peer median 14.7x — and ranking P0 (cheapest in sector) on forward P/E and P17 on EV/EBITDA — TCS screens unambiguously cheap on live ratios, a discount warranted partly by scale but also a genuine valuation anomaly at the 52-week low. The primary risk is that CC growth remains near-zero or negative in FY27 as AI automation deflates legacy T&M volumes faster than the $40B TCV pipeline converts to recognised revenue, leaving INR growth a currency-translation artefact rather than real business expansion.

fundamental.thesis: Sun Pharma is India's #1 pharma company by revenue with a diversified model spanning branded generics (~46% of sales), innovative medicines (~20%), US generics (~30%), and a growing global biosimilars franchise (#7 worldwide, 8 products in market); it also commands a net-cash balance sheet of ₹26,220 cr and 14.4% revenue CAGR since FY10, making it the highest-quality name in the Indian pharma universe. Consolidated revenue grew +11.1% YoY in FY26, with domestic formulations accelerating from +10% in Q1FY26 to +16.2% in 9MFY26 — a clean positive trajectory — while the US segment (key earnings driver) stalled to near-flat growth of +0.6% YoY in 9MFY26, down from +1.4% in Q1FY26; PAT margin improved sequentially from 16.4% (Q1FY26) to 21.8% (9MFY26), though FY26 standalone data shows mixed signals and the trend table contains standalone/consolidated mixing that limits precise reading. At trailing P/E 37.4× (within the pharma sector median range of 28–40×) and EV/EBITDA of 24.2× (17% premium to peer median of 20.7×), the stock is FAIR — forward P/E of 27.7× signals earnings growth is priced in and broadly consistent with a company growing 11%+ on a ₹52,000 cr revenue base; the Organon women's health acquisition (guidance raised in Q1FY27) adds optionality but also integration risk, while the valuation snapshot D/E field of 5.52× appears to be a data error duplicating P/B — actual D/E per sector filings is 0.05, confirming a net-cash, low-leverage business. The single biggest risk is the US Commerce Department's mandated review of generic drug tariffs within one year — if extended beyond patented pharma to generics, roughly 30% of Sun Pharma's revenue faces material headwinds at a time when US revenue growth is already near-zero.

fundamental.thesis: Bajaj Finserv is India's largest diversified financial services holding company, operating through Bajaj Finance (NBFC with ₹5 lakh cr+ AUM), Bajaj Life Insurance (21% GWP growth in FY26), and Bajaj General Insurance (8% GWP growth), with the FY26 full buyout of Allianz's stake simplifying an historically complex group structure. FY26 consolidated revenue grew 13.2% YoY to ₹1,50,530 cr, but PAT margin contracted from 7.9% in Q1FY26 to 6.5% by full-year FY26 — a clear multi-quarter compression trend — while AUM growth decelerated from 26% to 22.4% and impairment on lending assets surged 33.6% YoY to ₹9,390 cr (1.88% of loans), which dominates the credit quality read even though reported GNPA improved to 1.01% at Q4FY26. Using P/B + ROE as the sector card yardstick for lenders: at P/B of 3.5× against ROE of 14.6%, the stock is in expensive territory on the rule-of-thumb (P/B > 3 is only defensible above ~15% ROE) and sits at P73 in sector on trailing P/E (28.2×, 61% premium to sector median 17.5×), though forward P/E of 18.7× signals earnings growth is priced in — overall fair, not cheap, given the franchise quality offset. The single biggest risk is that next-FY EPS estimates have been cut 11.5% over 90 days while impairments are rising and deposits contracted 4% even as the loan book grew 22%, a combination that could force higher provisioning, widen forward P/E materially, and trigger a re-rating down toward sector median.

FY26 consolidated revenue reached a lifetime high of ₹211,000 cr with India EBITDA margin at 51.2%; quarterly India revenue growth has held steady at 15–18% YoY (Q4FY26: +16%), but ARPU — the single most important sector KPI — has stalled at ₹257 in Q4FY26 (down from ₹259 in Q3FY26), well short of management's ₹300 target, and PAT fell -21% YoY in Q4FY26 to ₹2,670 cr, partly on base effects and international roaming headwinds. Using EV/EBITDA as the correct yardstick for this capital-intensive business (per sector card), 10.54× sits squarely in the fair range of 9–12× for India mobile; with the stock at only 15% of its 52-week range and forward P/E (21.6×) far below trailing (40.7×), the market is pricing in meaningful earnings growth, but this requires ARPU recovery which management itself flags as constrained at entry-level price points. fundamental.thesis: E.I.D. Parry is a diversified conglomerate anchored in sugar manufacturing and nutraceuticals (spirulina), and functions partly as a holding company for its stake in Coromandel International (fertilizers/crop protection), which drives much of its intrinsic value — a structure that makes the FMCG sector tag misleading and EBITDA/EV the correct valuation yardstick. Standalone revenue grew 21.9% YoY to ₹3,853 cr in FY26 and the prior three quarters showed sequential acceleration (Q1FY26 +29.3%, Q2FY26 +24.6%, Q3FY26 +18.3%), but consolidated PAT declined 35.1% to ₹570 cr due to ₹478+ cr in exceptional charges from the PSRIPL sugar refinery closure, financial guarantee provisions, and PP&E impairments; gross margins are visibly contracting (27.0% FY25 → 22.5% Q3FY26) and volume growth is decelerating (17.5% Q4FY25 → 10.0% Q1FY26), while full-year CFO/PAT collapsed to 0.02×, meaning reported earnings are not converting to cash. On EV/EBITDA of 5.63× the stock sits at the P2 percentile among 499 peers and at a 75% discount to the broad-market median — unambiguously cheap — but this discount is clearly structural: extreme leverage (D/E 23.65), a zero-cash-conversion earnings base, a closed sugar refinery requiring post-year equity infusion of ~₹610 cr, and sharp 30-day EPS estimate cuts of −26% all point to a value trap rather than a mispriced compounder. The single biggest risk is that ongoing sugar-segment restructuring, combined with extreme balance sheet leverage, forces equity dilution and further exceptional charges before the Coromandel holding value can be unlocked.

Using the Sector Card yardstick of P/B vs ROE for lenders, P/B of 1.35× with a TTM ROE of only 4.9% is deeply unimpressive — a bank earning sub-5% ROE warranting P/B above 1× only if recovery is imminent; for context, a healthy private bank with 15%+ ROE commands 2.5–3.5× P/B, so the current multiple prices in meaningful recovery that has not yet materialised, grading this as 'fair' to slightly expensive on a quality-adjusted basis. Q2FY26 delivered consolidated revenue of ₹3,324 cr (+47.5% YoY) and PAT of ₹1,430 cr (+36.2% YoY) at a 43% PAT margin, reflecting an ongoing LME aluminium price recovery cycle; however, EBITDA margins show a mild contracting trend (46.9% in FY25 → 42.3% in Q1FY26, recovering to 45.6% in H1FY26), and cash conversion remains strong at 1.10× CFO/PAT. Using EV/EBITDA as the correct yardstick for this capital-intensive cyclical (per sector card; P/E is misleading for commodity names), NALCO's 7.39× sits at the upper end of the 5–8× mid-cycle cyclical range, yet ranks at P5 out of 471 broad-market peers on EV/EBITDA and P8 on trailing P/E (11×, well below the 12–22× Materials median), making valuation appear cheap on both absolute and relative bases with estimate revisions tracking strongly upward (+20.2% over 90 days). The overriding risk is a sharp LME aluminium price reversal driven by a Chinese supply surge or demand slowdown, compounded by DXY strengthening (currently 100.8) which simultaneously erodes USD-denominated realisations with no pricing-power buffer available to NALCO.
